public_rationale: Microsoft confirms that its AI business surpassed a $37 billion annual revenue run rate. The reviewed usable evidence does not establish how that figure divides between OpenAI compute, Copilot, and other business. Comparing later full-year OpenAI revenue with the March run rate would mix periods and measurement bases. The aggregate figure therefore does not validate the asserted composition.
limitations: The relevant composition was not established as publicly known by the evaluation date.
The Bloomberg page was an incomplete preview and was excluded.
The Copilot estimate is hedged and uses a potentially different revenue measure.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Microsoft's $37 billion AI annual run rate is mostly OpenAI's compute, with the rest, maybe $8 billion a year at best, coming from pushing customers to install Copilot.

statement.excerpt: Microsoft’s $37 billion in AI annual run rate — these fucking cowards never share actual AI revenues! — is predominantly made up of OpenAI’s compute, with the rest of it (maybe $8 billion in annual revenue at best) from Microsoft harassing its permanently-abused customer base into installing Copilot.

from_speaker: Microsoft’s $37 billion in AI annual run rate
predominantly made up of OpenAI’s compute
maybe $8 billion in annual revenue at best
our_interpretation: The target period is Microsoft's fiscal third quarter ending March 31, 2026, the latest reported quarter before the post.
'Predominantly' means more than half of the stated AI revenue run rate.
The claim attributes the remainder to Copilot. Copilot is read broadly because the sentence does not identify a particular Copilot product.
The $8 billion figure is explicitly tentative. It is assessed as an estimate, not an unconditional numerical ceiling.
Annual realized revenue cannot be divided by a point-in-time annualized run rate to establish a customer share.
The pejorative description of selling Copilot is not a separate measurable proposition.
criteria.support_condition: A compatible breakdown of the fiscal-third-quarter AI revenue run rate shows that OpenAI compute accounts for more than half and Copilot accounts for the remainder, with any $8 billion estimate reconciled to its stated measurement basis.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A compatible breakdown shows OpenAI compute at half or less, or shows a material remainder attributable to products or customers outside Copilot.
